questions.q: Why does Oracle Fusion offer a guided Accounting Configuration Manager flow instead of only isolated setup tasks?
options: Because building a primary ledger with its legal entities and business units together is such a common combination that a connected flow reduces the chance of a missed link
Because legal entities cannot exist without this tool
Because the chart of accounts is created inside this tool only
Because isolated tasks are technically impossible to complete
questions.explain: The guided flow exists because this combination of pieces is configured together so often, and configuring them in isolation makes it easy to forget a required connection.

questions.q: In the guided sequence, what comes immediately after creating the primary ledger and before assigning legal entities?
options: Assigning business units
Specifying ledger options such as sequencing, rounding, and journal approval rules
Running the trial balance report
Defining cross-validation rules
questions.explain: The sequence runs: create the primary ledger, specify ledger options, then assign legal entities, then assign balancing segment values.

questions.q: What do 'ledger options' generally refer to, as distinct from 'accounting options'?
options: The currency conversion rate type used company-wide
The cross-validation rules applied to journal entries
The operational settings of the ledger itself, such as sequencing and rounding rules
Only the chart of accounts structure
questions.explain: Ledger options cover the ledger's own operational settings; accounting options generally refer to subledger accounting behavior for that ledger.

questions.q: What does assigning a legal entity to a primary balancing segment value enable?
options: It merges all legal entities into one combined balance
It has no practical effect on reporting
It allows the legal entity to skip statutory reporting
It allows a single ledger to produce a separate, in-balance trial balance per legal entity
questions.explain: The legal-entity-to-balancing-segment-value link is what lets one ledger keep each legal entity's financial position cleanly separated and in balance.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what happens if the legal-entity-to-balancing-segment assignment is skipped or misconfigured?
options: Nothing changes; it is a purely cosmetic setting
The ledger can no longer cleanly separate one legal entity's financial position from another's
The chart of accounts automatically regenerates
The primary ledger is deleted automatically
questions.explain: Misconfiguring this link defeats much of the purpose of multi-entity accounting, since the ledger can no longer separate entities' balances cleanly.
